text:
Juuse Saros ended Carolina's four-game winning streak by making 29 saves on a night the Hurricanes had the better of the play. Nashville won 4-1 on the strength of its goalie, who stopped 2.6 goals more than the quality of those shots should have allowed. Saros was drafted 99th overall in 2013 out of HPK in Finland, and on this night he looked like the first-round talent Central Scouting once saw.

Our numbers say Carolina deserved better. The Hurricanes took 72 shot attempts to Nashville's 54 and out-chanced the Predators 1.42 to 0.42 in expected goals (a measure of shot quality) in the first period. Expected goals finished nearly even, 3.56 for CAR and 3.53 for NSH, but in the simulated replays of every shot, CAR wins 62 percent of the time. Pyotr Kochetkov was a bit worse than the chances he faced, allowing three goals against 2.79 expected.

Nashville took what it got. Nick Perbix and Roman Josi scored in the first two periods, both assisted by Filip Forsberg, before Jackson Blake pulled Carolina within one. Adam Edstrom's tip-in made it 3-1 early in the third, and Ross Colton sealed it at 19:19 with a 74 percent chance. The Hurricanes now have to find a new streak after losing for the first time in five games, while Nashville leaves with a win built on one goalie's night.
